For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi$ with $\chi_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi/2,\pi$ and at $\chi_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $\chi_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $\Lambda\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2\chi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.

hep-ph.title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
hep-ph.author: Francesco Bertucci, James Bonifacio, Andrew Schrader
hep-ph.abstract: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

hep-ph.title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
hep-ph.author: Vishnu Jejjala, Damian Mayorga Pena
hep-ph.abstract: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.

hep-ph.title: NuSrcAgent: An AI Agent for High-Energy Neutrino Source Searches
hep-ph.author: Bei Zhou, Po-Wen Chang, Kohta Murase
hep-ph.abstract: Identifying the sources of high-energy cosmic neutrinos is crucial for understanding cosmic particle accelerators and probing new physics. IceCube provides public data that allow researchers to search independently for neutrino sources, but these analyses require substantial technical expertise and careful scientific choices. We present \system, the first publicly available AI agent for high-energy neutrino source searches. Compared to public likelihood codes, \system is easier to install and use, and supports more analysis types. To start an analysis, users need only specify a source or catalog. The agent takes natural-language requests, runs likelihood analyses on public IceCube event data, and saves the settings and calculation records so users can repeat the analyses. We demonstrate \system through single-source and catalog stacking analyses, obtaining results consistent with IceCube results. These examples also show its ability to search the literature, analyze non-power-law spectra using user-provided model code, and develop new analysis functions, such as signal-injection simulations. \system is also a powerful tool for improving and testing existing analysis code, as we demonstrate by using it to refine the background probability density functions and reduce residuals and spurious signal contributions in stacking analyses. \system makes high-energy neutrino data analysis more accessible to the broader research community. Code and usage instructions: \href{this https URL}{\faGithub\ {\ttthis http URL}}.

hep-ph.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
hep-ph.author: Xiu-Lei Ren
hep-ph.abstract: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

hep-ph.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
hep-ph.author: Mauricio Bustamante
hep-ph.abstract: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $\nu_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.

hep-ph.title: Time-weighted energy correlators are infrared unsafe in gauge theories
hep-ph.author: Siqing Yu
hep-ph.abstract: Energy correlators are infrared safe because each detector weights a parton by its energy, but a weight in the arrival time makes them infrared unsafe in gauge theories. For the state created by a scalar operator that makes two partons at lowest order in a weakly coupled conformal gauge theory, we show that the correlator of two time-weighted energy detectors (the light-ray operators $\int\!du\,u\,T_{uu}$) at separated directions diverges at two loops like the logarithm of the time window. The logarithm does not come from a single soft gluon, but from a soft parton pair with comparable energies, one parton in each detector; its coefficient is a closed-form function of the angle for any matter content. In $N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, we recover this coefficient from the two-gluon Regge term of the known four-point function and derive a simple relation to the logarithm in the charge correlator. In the planar theory the leading logarithms resum to a power of the window, set by the BFKL intercept.

hep-ph.title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
hep-ph.author: Taushif Ahmed, Syed Mehedi Hasan
hep-ph.abstract: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.

hep-ph.title: Resonant top pair searches at the LHC: a window to electroweak phase transition
hep-ph.author: Dorival Gonçalves, Ajay Kaladharan, Yongcheng Wu
hep-ph.abstract: The dynamics of electroweak phase transition could have profound consequences for particle physics and cosmology. We study the prospects for the HL-LHC to probe the strong first-order electroweak phase transition (SFOEWPT) regime in the type-I 2HDM. We focus on the Higgstrahlung channel $pp\to ZH/A$ with a resonant top-quark pair final state $H/A\to t\bar t$. We find that the top-quark pair final state renders the largest sensitivity to the SFOEWPT regime, in comparison to the other Higgstrahlung searches already performed by ATLAS and CMS, that focus on the $H/A\to bb$ and $H\to WW$ final states. We also derive the complementarity of the Higgstrahlung searches with other relevant classes of searches at the HL-LHC and compare them with the gravitational wave sensitivity at LISA.

hep-ph.title: Hadrons in group expansion
hep-ph.author: Hua-Xing Chen
hep-ph.abstract: We develop a general framework for describing symmetry-breaking responses in physical systems with approximate symmetries. Hadronic systems provide a particularly rich setting for investigating such symmetries. For example, the flavor $SU(4)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, $s$, and $c$ quarks is severely broken, the flavor $SU(3)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, and $s$ quarks is moderately broken, and the isospin $SU(2)$ symmetry involving the $u$ and $d$ quarks is only slightly broken. An important question is how a physical system responds to further symmetry breaking when its symmetry has already been partially broken. Motivated by the observed mass nonadditivity of vector mesons, we formulate this framework in terms of the group expansion, in which higher-order responses may modify the coefficients within the inherited response space or unlock additional independent response directions outside this space. We refer to these two effects as coefficient evolution and response unlocking, respectively, and develop a differential description connecting the interaction flow, mass flow, and state flow. We apply this framework to $J^P=1^-$ vector mesons and $J^P=3/2^+$ and $1/2^+$ baryons within flavor $SU(4)$ and $SU(5)$ reference spaces. These analyses illustrate how the internal structure and dynamics of a physical system, together with additional symmetries, can shape and constrain its symmetry-breaking responses. The group expansion thus provides a unified framework for organizing the evolution, correlations, and constraints of symmetry-breaking responses, with potential applications beyond hadronic systems.

hep-ph.title: Study of anomalous charged triple gauge couplings with $W^-W^+$ process at $e^-e^+$ collider
hep-ph.author: Amir Subba, Ritesh K. Singh
hep-ph.abstract: We study anomalous charged triple gauge couplings (aTGC) in $e^-e^+\to W^-W^+$ at $\sqrt{s}=250$~GeV with longitudinally polarized beams, parameterized by the five dimension-six operators $\mathcal{O}_{WWW}$, $\mathcal{O}_{W}$, $\mathcal{O}_{B}$, $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{W}WW}$ and $\mathcal{O}_{\widetilde{W}}$ of the HISZ basis. All three decay channels, $\ell^\pm jj\slashed{E}$, $4j$ and $\ell^-\ell^+\slashed{E}$, are simulated explicitly at a leading-order including all diagrams that contribute to each final state and hence the interference of $W^-W^+$ with non-resonant amplitudes. The semi-leptonic signal is selected with cuts on $m_{j_1j_2}$ and $m_T^W$. The flavor identity of the two hardest light jets are classified as \emph{up}-type and \emph{down}-type jets with a dedicated boosted decision trees (BDT). In the $4j$ channel a multi-class BDT separates $W^-W^+$ from $ZZ$ and QCD production and the $W^\pm$ candidates are assigned using jet charge. In the dilepton channel $W^-W^+$ events are selected with cuts on $p_T^{\ell^-}$ and $m_{\ell^-\ell^+}$, and the two neutrino momenta are reconstructed analytically from the on-shell and beam-energy constraints. The cross section and 80 polarization and spin-correlation asymmetries in four disjoint bins of $\cos\theta_{W^-}$ are combined for both beam-polarization configurations through a covariance-based $\chi^2$. The two set of beam polarization offers an orthogonal cuts on parameter space leading to tighter bounds. The semi-leptonic and full-hadronic final states provides a competitive bounds on aTGCs, while full-leptonic offers the least sensitivity. Marginalized limits on aTGCs via. Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis for integrated luminosities for different values of integrated luminosities and systematic benchmarks are reported.

hep-ph.title: Lindblad-driven recombination of the X(3872) tetraquark
hep-ph.author: Néstor Armesto, Miguel Ángel Escobedo, Elena G. Ferreiro, Víctor López-Pardo
hep-ph.abstract: The internal structure of the exotic meson X(3872) remains an open question. We investigate its production in heavy-ion collisions under the hypothesis that it is a compact tetraquark. To this end, we derive a coalescence model from the Lindblad equation, assuming that unbound heavy quarks are thermalized within the quark-gluon plasma and that the adiabatic approximation holds. Using this model, we predict the nuclear modification factor of the X(3872) at LHC energies, with proton-proton baseline cross sections estimated from available experimental data. We also consider the effect of simplifying assumptions on the model, and a complementary approach based on chemical equilibration. Our results indicate that recombination is the dominant production mechanism for a tetraquark X(3872). It leads to a significant yield enhancement in heavy-ion collisions, suggesting that the nuclear modification factor is a powerful observable for probing the exotic nature of this state

hep-ph.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward di-hadron correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
hep-ph.author: Paul Caucal, Zhong-Bo Kang, Piotr Korcyl, Farid Salazar, Björn Schenke, Tomasz Stebel, Raju Venugopalan, Wenbin Zhao
hep-ph.abstract: We present a detailed numerical investigation of semi-inclusive forward di-hadron production in proton--nucleus collisions employing the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. We focus on the regime where di-hadrons are produced nearly back-to-back in the transverse plane, thereby justifying a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization approach in terms of small-$x$ gluon distributions. Our computation integrates several key elements: i) non-linear rapidity evolution via the Balitsky--Kovchegov equation with running coupling, ii) both perturbative and non-perturbative Sudakov resummation, and iii) a phenomenologically constrained model for the initial conditions for small-$x$ gluon distributions. We compare this phenomenological framework to experimental data from the STAR Collaboration on azimuthal correlations in forward di-pion production in both proton--proton and proton--gold collisions. We analyze the systematic theoretical uncertainties associated with the saturation scales of nuclei at the initial scale for rapidity evolution and with those associated with the hadronization process. Finally, we make predictions for the kinematics anticipated to be covered by the ALICE Forward Calorimeter (FoCal) upgrade at the Large Hadron Collider.

hep-ph.title: Critical fluctuation patterns and anisotropic correlations driven by temperature gradients
hep-ph.author: Lijia Jiang, Tao Yang, Jun-Hui Zheng
hep-ph.abstract: Studies of QCD phase transition signals are often conducted under spatially uniform temperature conditions. However, the influence of spatial temperature gradients on the signals emerging at the phase interface in the fireball generated by heavy-ion collisions has not yet been fully explored. Based on an Ising-like effective potential, we study the locally equilibrated systems with temperature gradients. In a 2D disk geometry, the low-energy fluctuation spectrum is explicitly resolved into radial and angular momentum modes. The nonlocal correaltions of singular eigen-mode exhibits strong anisotropy, which are long-ranged along isotherms but suppressed radially due to the thermal geometry of the system. Unlike homogeneous systems where the zero-momentum mode dominates, correlations in such inhomogeneous system result from the superposition of a series of zero and non-zero angular momentum modes with comparable contributions. We extract the singular angular momentum modes and establish their connection to experimentally observable anisotropic flow. We find azimuthally sensitive observables may offer a previously unexplored avenue for detecting the QCD phase transition.

hep-ph.title: Dark matter in classically conformal theories: WIMP and supercooling
hep-ph.author: Ke-Pan Xie, Cheng-Hao Zhan
hep-ph.abstract: Beyond solving the hierarchy problem, classically conformal (CC) theories naturally accommodate dark matter (DM). In this work, we explore the CC $SU(2)_X$ gauge theory with a triplet dark scalar, uncovering two distinct DM scenarios: weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) and supercooled DM. The production mechanisms are strongly influenced by the CC model's unique first-order phase transition evolution history, which differs significantly from those in non-conformal models. We obtain the viable parameter space for each scenario and investigate the current constraints and future sensitivities at experiments, demonstrating that gravitational wave signals from the phase transition provide a common detection channel for both the WIMP and supercooled DM regimes.

hep-ph.title: Light-by-light scattering: asymptotic expansions, Coulomb resummation and NLO corrections
hep-ph.author: Ajjath A H, Ekta Chaubey, Hua-Sheng Shao
hep-ph.abstract: Light-by-light (LbL) scattering is one of the earliest predictions of quantum electrodynamics (QED). Interest in this process has been renewed following its experimental observation at the LHC and the prospects of future measurements at free-electron laser facilities. In this paper, we refine theoretical predictions for LbL scattering by improving the full fermion-mass-dependent two-loop QCD and QED helicity amplitudes using high- and low-energy asymptotic expansions, and by performing Coulomb resummation in the threshold region. The $W$-boson contribution, relevant when the di-photon invariant mass exceeds twice the $W$-boson mass, is included at one-loop accuracy. We present state-of-the-art predictions for LbL cross sections in the Standard Model and provide a new event generator, LbLatNLO, for Monte Carlo simulations of LbL scattering.

hep-ph.title: Higgs production in association with a Z boson at TeV-scale lepton colliders
hep-ph.author: Hiroyuki Furusato, Satsuki Hosoya, Kentarou Mawatari, Shouta Suzuki

hep-ph.title: Matter-wave Interferometers as Open-system Dark Matter Detectors
hep-ph.author: Leonardo Badurina, Kathryn M. Zurek
hep-ph.abstract: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) offer a uniquely quantum route to dark matter (DM) detection: DM can reveal itself through phase and decoherence between spatially separated wavepackets, even when energy deposition is negligible and no resolvable recoil displacement occurs. We formulate these effects in an open effective field theory for MWIs using the Schwinger--Keldysh formalism, which highlights a structural asymmetry between the two detection channels. For elastic spin-independent DM scattering, decoherence inherits novel Bose enhancement or Pauli blocking factors, while the phase is at most linear in the DM occupation number. By retaining the DM's coherence time, this framework spans Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics across a wide range of DM masses, and systematically organizes corrections beyond the heavy-probe limit.

hep-ph.title: $D^0$-$D_s^+$ Elliptic-Flow Splitting under Event-Shape Engineering: A Probe of Sequential Charm Hadronization
hep-ph.author: Yu-Jie Huang, Wei Dai, Jiaxing Zhao, Tan Luo, Ben-Wei Zhang, Enke Wang
hep-ph.abstract: Recent work has proposed sequential hadronization of open-charm hadrons in the quark-gluon plasma, wherein more tightly bound species such as $D_s^+$ form earlier near $1.2 T_c$ and $D^0$ forms later at $T_c$. That work showed that this mechanism naturally reverses the sign of the $D^0-D_s^+$ elliptic-flow splitting relative to the conventional simultaneous baseline. In this work, we demonstrate that event-shape engineering (ESE) provides a sharper discrimination between the two pictures than inclusive measurements alone. By selecting large-$q_2$ and small-$q_2$ events in 0--10\% and 30--50\% centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV, we show that the geometry-driven enhancement of charm-meson $v_2$ can be separated from the hadronization-time response: the positive $\Delta v_2(D^0-D_s^+)$ in the sequential scenario grows systematically with $q_2$, while the corresponding response slope $\chi$ reveals a species-dependent hierarchy $\chi(D^0) > \chi(D_s^+)$ that is robust against the overall flow normalization and absent in the simultaneous baseline. In the simultaneous case, the splitting is near zero or negative and does not follow the same geometry scaling. Notably, the semi-central 30--50\% class emerges as the optimal window, because the non-monotonic interplay between QGP lifetime and initial eccentricity maximizes the late-stage flow conversion. The $q_2$ ratios of the $D_s^+/D^0$ yield ratio remain close to unity, confirming that the splitting is a dynamical flow effect rather than a chemical yield modification. These results establish $\Delta v_2(D^0-D_s^+)$ and the response slope $\chi$ under ESE as complementary differential probes of the space-time structure of charm hadronization near the QCD transition temperature.

hep-ph.title: Electroweak First-Order Phase Transition Triggered by Non-Gaussian Fluctuations of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Symmetric Spectator Scalar
hep-ph.author: Bo-Qiang Lu
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a novel mechanism to trigger a first-order cosmological electroweak phase transition using non-Gaussian primordial fluctuations of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spectator scalar field. We show that the large fluctuations of the spectator field can modify the Higgs thermal mass and enhance the thermal barrier, thereby enabling a strong first-order phase transition. Non-Gaussianities in the primordial fluctuation spectrum significantly increase the probability of large-amplitude fluctuations, allowing a substantial fraction of the Universe to undergo the transition. The spectator field also naturally serves as a cold dark matter candidate through its coherent oscillations, reproducing the observed relic abundance. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background peaks at $f\sim 10^{-3}-10^{-1}$ Hz, but its amplitude lies roughly ten orders of magnitude below the projected sensitivities of planned space-based and ground-based interferometers.

hep-ph.title: QCD sum-rule determination of the axial-vector mixing angle in the \(B_c(1P)\) sector
hep-ph.author: T.M. Aliev, S. Bilmis, M. Savci
hep-ph.abstract: We determine the mixing angle between the \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\) axial-vector states in the \(B_c(1P)\) sector using QCD sum rules. The operator product expansion includes the gluon condensates and the four-quark condensate up to dimension six, and the next-to-leading-order perturbative corrections to all three correlation functions; for the correlator of the axial-vector and tensor currents these corrections are calculated here for the first time. The analysis of the sum rules leads to \(\theta_{B_c(1P)}=(46.6\pm0.4)^\circ\) for the mixing angle between these two states. We also compare our result with theoretical studies available in the literature.

hep-ph.title: $λ$, $ρ$, and $σ$ Regge trajectories for the quadruply heavy pentaquark $bb\bar{u}cc$ in the diquark-triquark picture
hep-ph.author: Xin-Ru Liu, Qi Liu, Jiao-Kai Chen
hep-ph.abstract: Systematic investigations of four series of Regge trajectories for quadruply heavy pentaquarks are still lacking. Using the diquark and triquark Regge trajectory relations, we propose the Regge trajectory relations for the quadruply heavy pentaquark ${bb\bar{u}cc}$: $M=2m_{b}+2m_{c}+m_{u}+5C/2 +\beta_{x_{\lambda}}(x_{\lambda}+c_{0x_{\lambda}})^{2/3} +\beta_{x_{\rho_1}}(x_{\rho_1}+c_{0x_{\rho_1}})^{2/3}+\beta_{x_{\rho_2}}\sqrt{x_{\rho_2}+c_{0x_{\rho_2}}} +\beta_{x_{\sigma}}(x_{\sigma}+c_{0x_{\sigma}})^{2/3}$. Four series of Regge trajectories, namely the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories, are investigated. We demonstrate that accounting for the internal structure and substructure of pentaquarks is indispensable for constructing the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories; without such structural considerations, functional form and trajectory parameters can only be obtained via pure fitting against theoretical or experimental data. We further prove that the Regge trajectories of diquark 1, triquark, and diquark 2 (embedded within the triquark) do not correspond one to one to the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories. Nevertheless, these trajectories govern the behaviors of the respective $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories. For both configurations $(bb)(\bar{u}(cc))$ and $(cc)(\bar{u}(bb))$, the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, and $\sigma$-trajectories exhibit behavior of $M{\sim}x^{2/3}$ ($x=n_{r_1},n_{r_3},l_1,l_3,N_{r},L$), whereas the $\rho_2$-trajectories exhibit behavior of $M{\sim}\sqrt{x}$ ($x=n_{r_2},\,l_2$). The functional behavior of Regge trajectories for diquarks and triquark offers guidance for fitting the pentaquark Regge trajectories. Additionally, we provide rough estimates for spin-averaged masses of the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, and $\sigma$-excited states.

hep-ph.title: Mathematical inverse problem for the world data inference of the parton distribution functions of the proton
hep-ph.author: Henri Hänninen
hep-ph.abstract: We show that the inference problem of constraining the parton distribution functions of the proton from deeply inelastic scattering data can be formulated as a linear tensor reconstruction inverse problem. This means that instead of fitting model parameters to the world data, a reconstructive approach to solve a system of coupled linear functional integral equations can be formulated. We leverage the mathematical structures of the integral equations defined by perturbative QCD and global analysis to pose the problem of global analysis as a coupled system of linear integral equations, and construct a proof-of-principle methodology to solve it. To formulate this approach concretely, we review all next-to-leading order accuracy results for inclusive virtual photon, neutral current, charged current, heavy flavor production, and neutrino deep-inelastic lepton--proton scattering. This mathematical methodology of inference opens a path towards a parametrization-bias-free extraction of the proton PDFs from the world data of deeply inelastic scattering in the spirit of indirect measurement employed in mathematical inverse problems, including robust estimation of uncertainties with reduced bias from model parametrization, while closely adhering to the established paradigm of perturbative QCD and global analysis.

hep-ph.title: Compositeness and decay properties of the flavor partner of $D^{*}_{s0}(2317)$
hep-ph.author: J. Sánchez-Illana, R. Molina, Pan-Pan Shi
hep-ph.abstract: In view of the recent experimental finding of the heavy quark flavor partner of the $D_{s0}(2317)$ in the bottom sector, the $B_{s0}(5700)$, we perform a single and coupled-channel $B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{(*)}$ calculation in the hidden-gauge formalism within the on-shell and off-shell schemes, respectively. By fixing the $B\bar{K}$ bound state mass to the observed state with $J^P=0^+$, we also predict five new states with $J^P=\lbrace 0,1,2\rbrace^+$ in this sector, three of them with $J^P=1^+$. Additionally, in the coupled-channel calculation, two states with masses and decay widths similar to the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ and $B_{sJ}(6063)$ ones, with spins $J=0^+$ and $2^+$, respectivley, and decaying into $B\bar{K}$, are dynamically generated. Moreover, we evaluate the decay widths of the $B_{s0}$ and $B_{s1}$ states generated from $B^{(*)}\bar{K}$ through the isospin breaking decay mode $B_s^0\pi^0$ and $B_s^{*0}\pi^0$, respectively. We find that, because these states have large binding energies, the coupling to the bare component can reduce this decay width by more than half of the decay width, from $50$~keV in the purely molecular model to $10-20$~keV, when the $B_{s0}$ is coupled to the bare component. We also observe that, after considering heavy-quark-spin symmetry violating contributions, the decay width for the $B_{s1}$ becomes smaller than for the $B_{s0}$.

hep-ph.title: Revealing irregularities through distributional discrepancies in latent space via Stein-witness estimation
hep-ph.author: Ali Eren Simsek
hep-ph.abstract: RIDDLE is a new method for resonant anomaly detection that uses a scalar Stein-witness function to identify discrepancies between unlabeled signal-region events and a background distribution inferred from dijet-mass sidebands. The witness is optimized in a latent representation of auxiliary jet observables against a differentiable background reference, without requiring an explicit signal model. The method is evaluated using simulated LHC Olympics dijet events and compared with its idealized and supervised benchmarks, which share the same statistical construction but use additional background or signal information, and with LaCATHODE as an independent anomaly detection method. RIDDLE demonstrates strong signal-background discrimination comparable to the idealized benchmark, generally outperforming LaCATHODE while largely preserving the background dijet-mass spectrum under anomaly-score selection. Tests incorporating additional angular information and deliberately mass-correlated features further demonstrate the method's robustness under the studied conditions. Together, these results highlight the potential of RIDDLE as a robust, data-driven approach for enhanced resonance searches that combines effective anomaly discrimination with background-shape preservation.

hep-ph.title: Parton Branching evolution in updfevolv: NNLO spacelike evolution in the ZM-VFNS and NLO timelike evolution with heavy-flavour matching
hep-ph.author: H. Jung
hep-ph.abstract: We describe two extensions of the Parton Branching (PB) method as implemented in updfevolv: the next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) spacelike DGLAP evolution of parton densities in the zero-mass variable-flavour-number scheme (ZM-VFNS), and the leading and next-to-leading order (LO, NLO) timelike evolution of fragmentation functions, including the heavy-flavour matching conditions at the quark thresholds. We summarise the timelike PB formalism - momentum sum rule, Sudakov form factor, branching chain and kinematics. We give implementation details needed for the PB formalism to reproduce the semi-analytical solutions of APFEL for all flavours, including heavy quarks at threshold. This note supplements the updfevolv manual and is a technical release note for updfevolv version 2.6.0.

hep-ph.title: Smooth binary evolution from wide resonances in boson clouds
hep-ph.author: Giovanni Maria Tomaselli
hep-ph.abstract: Ultralight scalars can form superradiant clouds around rotating black holes. These may alter the dynamics of compact binaries and the ensuing waveform through orbital resonances and cloud ionization. We re-examine resonances involving states with nonzero decay width, deriving an effective treatment for resonances that are wider than the binary's frequency chirp. We demonstrate the utility of this approach by calculating an upper bound for the cloud's mass surviving up to the latest stages of the inspiral. Next, we study the accumulation of resonances with high-energy bound states. When these infinitely many, increasingly weak resonances are properly taken into account, they smooth out the "sharp features" in the binary's evolution that had been attributed to the ionization of the cloud. We compare our Newtonian results with recent relativistic calculations, highlighting common features as well as discrepancies. Our conclusions emphasize the need to carefully incorporate resonances in boson cloud waveform modeling.

hep-ph.title: Electromagnetic Radiation from Baryon-Rich Matter in Heavy-Ion Collisions
hep-ph.author: Xiang-Yu Wu, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Jean-François Paquet, Björn Schenke, Chun Shen
hep-ph.abstract: We perform a study of electromagnetic radiation in heavy-ion collisions at Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) Beam Energy Scan (BES) and SPS energies using the iEBE-MUSIC framework, which includes 3D dynamical Monte Carlo Glauber initial conditions, MUSIC (3+1)D viscous relativistic hydrodynamics, and the UrQMD hadronic afterburner. The multistage modeling has been calibrated to hadronic data at RHIC-BES energies using a Bayesian analysis. Integrating the thermal photon emission rates with the medium evolution, we study the direct photon yield and elliptic flow and how they vary with collision energy and emission source. We compare with results obtained by the STAR and PHENIX Collaborations. We employ next-to-leading order thermal QCD dilepton emission rates to compute dilepton invariant mass spectra and extract the effective temperature of the quark-gluon plasma at different collision energies.

hep-ph.title: Acoustic gravitational waves from primordial curvature perturbations
hep-ph.author: Zhuan Ning, Zi-Yan Yuwen, Xiang-Xi Zeng, Rong-Gen Cai, Shao-Jiang Wang
hep-ph.abstract: Standard perturbative calculations of scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have neglected nonperturbative effects in the large-amplitude regime. We develop a hybrid numerical framework to signify nonperturbative effects on the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background sourced by primordial curvature perturbations, focusing on the acoustic channel (fluid motions). Fully general-relativistic, spherically symmetric simulations are used to extract nonperturbative sound-shell profiles from isolated curvature peaks; these profiles are then embedded into three-dimensional lattice evolutions of relativistic hydrodynamics coupled to transverse-traceless metric perturbations to compute the acoustic GW spectra. The acoustic signal has a peak frequency determined by the comoving shell thickness, and its amplitude is extremely sensitive to the mean comoving separation of peaks, scaling approximately as $R_{*c}^{-7}$. We find a robust causal low-frequency tail $\propto k^{3}$, and the nonlinear hydrodynamic interactions can enhance the ultraviolet power. Comparing with SIGWs computed perturbatively from the same real-space configuration, we show that acoustic GWs can be amplified by an order of magnitude and display a peak shifted to a lower frequency in the large-amplitude regime. These results highlight the importance of nonperturbative effects for accurate predictions of stochastic GW signals induced from primordial curvature perturbations.

hep-ph.title: Weyl conformal geometry vs Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant (dressed) metric
hep-ph.author: D. M. Ghilencea, V.-M. Mandric
hep-ph.abstract: Weyl conformal geometry is the natural underlying geometry of gauge theories of Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincaré symmetry), such as Weyl quadratic gravity and its generalisation, Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). These are local, Weyl-anomaly free (quantum) gauge theories of gravity. We describe Weyl gauge symmetry from a more familiar Riemannian view of Weyl gauge invariant dressed fields by the Wilson line of dilatations. Weyl geometry can then be seen as Riemannian geometry of non-local dressed metric ($g_{\mu\nu}^*$), at the "cost" of (gauge-induced) non-commutativity in the UV, due to Wilson line. Then Weyl quadratic gravity and WDBI actions of Weyl geometry, which are Weyl gauge invariant in $d$ dimensions, have the same expression in Riemannian geometry defined by $g^*_{\mu\nu}$. This is a non-local map and dual description of the two geometries and actions in the symmetric phase. Unlike for the metric, the equation of motion of Weyl gauge field ($\omega_\mu$) does not commute with the dressing of the metric. Quantum non-locality, in particular entanglement, and non-commutativity are (gauge-invariant) physical artefacts of "translating" (local) Weyl geometry and Weyl gauge covariance into our real-world Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant observables, and they are evidence of Weyl gauge symmetry. At lower energies, $\omega_\mu$ becomes massive, can decouple and Einstein-Hilbert action and commutativity are recovered. The case of a light $\omega_\mu$ is also discussed.

hep-ph.title: The EEC-Hedron: Positivity Bounds on Energy Correlators
hep-ph.author: Bianka Meçaj, Ian Moult, Hidde Stoffels, Matthew T. Walters, Yuan Xin
hep-ph.abstract: We study the constraints placed by energy positivity on general unitary quantum field theories. We show that the coefficients in the partial wave expansion of energy-energy correlators all must lie within a bounded region of parameter space, which we call the "EEC-hedron". For the particular case of conformal field theories, these positivity constraints on energy correlators lead to bounds on the allowed values of coefficients in the operator product expansion. We demonstrate this approach in the 3d Ising and $O(2)$ CFTs, deriving new bounds on OPE coefficients in both theories.

hep-ph.title: HydróDex: gotta match 'em all!
hep-ph.author: Giulio Barni, Eric Madge
hep-ph.abstract: First-order phase transitions can source a stochastic gravitational-wave background within reach of LISA and other future detectors, with sound waves in the plasma typically providing the dominant contribution. Predicting the resulting gravitational-wave signal requires determining the stationary fluid profiles around expanding bubbles. We present a complete hydrodynamic classification of these profiles in the constant-sound-speed model, which generalizes the bag model by allowing the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the wall and evolving the surrounding plasma, we recover the known direct and inverse detonations, deflagrations, and hybrids, and uncover mixed hybrids, a new class with rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+>c_-$, multiple stationary profiles can correspond to the same wall velocity $\xi_w$ and asymptotic transition strength $\alpha_N$. This non-uniqueness arises because this parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We compute the kinetic-energy budget and acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed hybrids introduce no additional spectral feature and can be mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with substantially different fluid profiles. Finally, we release HydróDex, a public code implementing the complete classification, profile construction, energy-budget calculation, and gravitational-wave prediction.

hep-ph.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
hep-ph.author: Xiang-Yu Wu, Han Gao, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Ralf Rapp
hep-ph.abstract: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $\rho$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.

hep-lat.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
hep-lat.author: Xiu-Lei Ren
hep-lat.abstract: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

hep-lat.title: Unfreezing topology using out-of-equilibrium replica exchanges
hep-lat.author: C. Bonanno, A. Bulgarelli, E. Cellini, R. Dionisio, A. Nada, D. Panfalone, D. Vadacchino, L. Verzichelli
hep-lat.abstract: Parallel Tempering on Boundary Conditions (PTBC) mitigates topological freezing by exchanging configurations between replicas that interpolate between periodic and open boundaries on a small defect. We generalize PTBC by replacing the instantaneous swap with a short out-of-equilibrium protocol, in which the defect couplings of two replicas are exchanged gradually while the fields around the defect are updated. We show that the swap rate depends only on the average work spent along the out-of-equilibrium trajectory by virtue of Crooks' and Jarzynski's fluctuation relations. From the theoretical derivation of the scaling of the work as a function of the number of replicas, protocol length, and defect size, we predict the swap rate and the optimal protocol length. These predictions are tested in the $2d$ $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ model with $N=21$. The optimal setup agrees with the measured one, the total computational cost at fixed statistical precision decreases by $\gtrsim40\%$ with respect to standard PTBC for all explored lattice spacings, and the required number of replicas at fixed acceptance is halved.

hep-lat.title: Lattice gauge theory computation of $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections to the quarkonium potential
hep-lat.author: Michael Eichberg, Marc Wagner
hep-lat.abstract: We compute the static quark-antiquark potential and its $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections, i.e.\ the $1/m_Q$ potential and all $1/m_Q^2$ potentials, which can be expressed in terms of correlators of two field strength insertions, in SU(3) lattice gauge theory and provide parameterizations for quark-antiquark separations $0.2 \, \text{fm} \lesssim r \lesssim 0.7 \, \text{fm}$. The field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops are renormalized using gradient flow, which also leads to small statistical uncertainties. All potentials are extrapolated to zero flow time and, in contrast to previous lattice studies, to the continuum, using three lattice spacings and four flow times. The spin dependent potentials are matched to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at NLO and provided at $\mu = 3 \, \text{GeV}$. They can easily be converted to specific heavy quark masses, e.g.\ for Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory studies of quarkonium.

hep-lat.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
hep-lat.author: Jack Y. Araz, Yamil Cahuana Medrano, Peter L. Nguyen, Zhong-Bo Kang, Jian-Wei Qiu, David Richards, Nobuo Sato, Marco Zaccheddu, Jia-Yue Zhang
hep-lat.abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.

hep-lat.title: Compositeness and decay properties of the flavor partner of $D^{*}_{s0}(2317)$
hep-lat.author: J. Sánchez-Illana, R. Molina, Pan-Pan Shi
hep-lat.abstract: In view of the recent experimental finding of the heavy quark flavor partner of the $D_{s0}(2317)$ in the bottom sector, the $B_{s0}(5700)$, we perform a single and coupled-channel $B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{(*)}$ calculation in the hidden-gauge formalism within the on-shell and off-shell schemes, respectively. By fixing the $B\bar{K}$ bound state mass to the observed state with $J^P=0^+$, we also predict five new states with $J^P=\lbrace 0,1,2\rbrace^+$ in this sector, three of them with $J^P=1^+$. Additionally, in the coupled-channel calculation, two states with masses and decay widths similar to the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ and $B_{sJ}(6063)$ ones, with spins $J=0^+$ and $2^+$, respectivley, and decaying into $B\bar{K}$, are dynamically generated. Moreover, we evaluate the decay widths of the $B_{s0}$ and $B_{s1}$ states generated from $B^{(*)}\bar{K}$ through the isospin breaking decay mode $B_s^0\pi^0$ and $B_s^{*0}\pi^0$, respectively. We find that, because these states have large binding energies, the coupling to the bare component can reduce this decay width by more than half of the decay width, from $50$~keV in the purely molecular model to $10-20$~keV, when the $B_{s0}$ is coupled to the bare component. We also observe that, after considering heavy-quark-spin symmetry violating contributions, the decay width for the $B_{s1}$ becomes smaller than for the $B_{s0}$.

hep-lat.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
hep-lat.author: Sorato Nagao, Hiroshi Suzuki
hep-lat.abstract: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $\kappa_\tau\Bar{\psi}\sigma_{\mu\nu}F_{\mu\nu}\psi$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi (WT) identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$. Consequently, at any fixed point with a vanishing gauge coupling, the eigenvalue in the direction of the gauge coupling is exactly~$-\gamma_A^*$, and the gauge coupling is relevant if and only if the vacuum polarization makes~$\gamma_A^*$ negative. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields such a fixed point, with~$\gamma_A^*=-1$ and three relevant directions. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line eliminate it unless $N_f$ is at least several tens. For~$N_f=1$, a search over the whole plane of the Pauli coupling and the mass parameter in the subspace~$e_\tau=0$, where our flow equation is exactly of one-loop order, finds a single fixed point, at strong Pauli coupling and a finite mass parameter. Like one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell, it has a finite mass parameter and two relevant directions. At their fixed point, the gauge coupling is relevant. At ours, in contrast, $\gamma_A^*>0$, so that the gauge coupling is irrelevant, and the fixed point cannot provide a UV completion of QED with a nonzero charge. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$ on the critical surface connected to the Gaussian fixed point, $\kappa_\tau$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value proportional to~$e_\tau^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_\tau^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

hep-th.title: Quantum critical collapse to an extremal black hole
hep-th.author: Hugo Lange, Harvey S. Reall
hep-th.abstract: It has been emphasized recently that some extremal black holes are "critical" solutions, lying at the threshold between gravitational collapse and dispersion. We study the effect of quantum gravity on critical solutions for the collapse of a thin shell of charged dust. We consider the Hamiltonian that generates the shell equation of motion with respect to the exterior Killing time and coincides with the ADM energy on-shell. Near criticality, this Hamiltonian is shown to be canonically equivalent to that of a Liouville theory with negative potential. After quantization, this model predicts that a collapsing shell has a non-trivial probability of undergoing a quantum mechanical bounce when its energy above extremality is comparable to the "breakdown scale". The bounce probability approaches unity at extremality. Hence this model predicts that the critical surface in the classical theory is thickened quantum mechanically into a "critical layer". The probability density function for the black hole energy is suppressed below the breakdown scale in the same way as found recently by Turiaci and Wu.

hep-th.title: The black hole IR triangle for scalar QED
hep-th.author: Fabiano Feleppa, Nava Gaddam, Nico Groenenboom
hep-th.abstract: We construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level. In the covariant phase space of the near-horizon Maxwell field, the soft charge is a corner term. The memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along the generators. It is conjugate to the boundary gauge mode that labels the degenerate horizon vacua, and Gauss' law fixes it by the flux of charge through the horizon. The Noether flux of the residual gauge transformation through the stretched horizon is not conserved by the scattering, because charged matter crosses the stretched horizon in both directions. The flux with its matter part removed is the soft charge, which generates the large gauge transformation. Its Ward identity is equivalent to a soft photon theorem in every radiative partial wave, which we derive from the near-horizon Feynman rules and, where these do not control the emission, from the field equations at leading order. The main difference from null infinity is that on a stretched horizon both radial branches of the field are independent boundary data. The hard charge is a radial flux. With both branches present it weights each leg by the direction of its radial motion, and the soft factor is a sign per leg. The endpoint data on the two branches give two boundary observables, the time-integrated transverse magnetic and electric fields. The field radiated by a scattering process contributes only to the first, where it cancels the change in the Coulomb memory of the charges, so that the soft charge is conserved. A charge that crosses the horizon enters both. We also discuss the infrared divergence, the dressing of the external states, and the fate of the memory in the Hartle--Hawking state, where it performs a random walk driven by the Hawking radiation.

hep-th.title: The OPE of lines beyond CFT
hep-th.author: Jan Albert, Matthew Forslund, Alexandre Homrich
hep-th.abstract: We discuss the fusion of parallel line defects in theories defined by relevant deformations of a conformal fixed point. We propose an operator product expansion to describe this limit in terms of a Wilsonian effective action whose coefficients are computable in conformal perturbation theory around the UV. This allows one to fix, order by order, the fusion limit of correlation functions involving the defects, up to non-perturbative coefficients associated to correlation functions (condensates) on the fused defect. It thus generalizes the familiar OPE of local operators in QFT. As a non-perturbative test of our proposal, we consider the short-distance potential between two magnetic impurities in the $2d$ Ising model. We find excellent agreement between the OPE framework and DMRG extractions of the potential and condensates (the latter also computed exactly with integrability). In addition, we consider a number of solvable models to illustrate different features of the framework.

hep-th.title: The String Theory Photinoverse
hep-th.author: Andreas P. Braun, Thibaut Coudarchet, Arthur Hebecker, Joerg Jaeckel, Jonathan Steiner
hep-th.abstract: Type-IIB string compactifications typically give rise to a significant number of RR-photons. These are generically massless and do not possess any light charged states, making them `superhidden'. However, since supersymmetry is present at least at some high scale, corresponding `dark photinos' are also predicted. The kinetic mixing of the photons together with the SUSY breaking mass terms of the photinos makes the latter observable. We identify geometries in which the mixing is induced by Wilson lines and show that their expectation values are generically non-zero. As a result, most of the dark photinos, which are lighter than the visible sector SUSY breaking scale, mix significantly with the bino and hence couple to the Standard Model sufficiently strongly to leave potentially observable traces. In particular, volume modulus and inflaton decays generically induce a cosmological abundance of dark photinos that can explain dark matter. We find that the `natural Photinoverse dark matter parameter space' is already accessible to current experiments, notably gamma ray observations, which therefore have discovery potential in the near future.

hep-th.title: Gauge groups of type 0 orientifolds
hep-th.author: Vittorio Larotonda, Salvatore Raucci
hep-th.abstract: We determine the global form of the gauge groups of the orthogonal and symplectic type 0 orientifolds, using the constraints from perturbative and brane states. In the process, we correct some misprints in type 0 vacuum amplitudes that have propagated in the literature. For type 0A, our analysis reveals a parity condition on the numbers of D9-branes in the orthogonal orientifold and a puzzle concerning the decay of a tachyonic D0-brane in the symplectic orientifold.

hep-th.title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
hep-th.author: Francesco Bertucci, James Bonifacio, Andrew Schrader
hep-th.abstract: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

hep-th.title: Neural Network Field Theory and the AdS/CFT Correspondence
hep-th.author: Dmitry S. Ageev, Yulia A. Ageeva, Anna S. Bernakevich
hep-th.abstract: We develop a neural realization of massive scalar field theory on Euclidean anti--de Sitter space and its holographic boundary observables within neural network field theory (NN--FT). We construct Fourier--Bessel cosine neurons whose covariance reproduces the regulated massive AdS propagator exactly at finite network width, with the Gaussian field theory recovered in the infinite-width limit.We introduce quartic interactions through two complementary approaches. The first implements a prescribed interaction by deforming the neural parameter measure, while the second generates a local quartic interaction from the statistics of auxiliary binary neurons. Applying the BDHM prescription directly to the neural ensemble, we recover the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, the conformal boundary two-point function, and the leading connected four-point contact Witten diagram.We further show that distinct neural architectures can reproduce the same leading boundary correlators while defining inequivalent bulk theories. These results establish a framework for studying interacting scalar holography within NN--FT and clarify the role of neural architecture in encoding bulk dynamics and boundary observables.

hep-th.title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
hep-th.author: Dmitry S. Ageev, Vladimir A. Bykov
hep-th.abstract: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. Finally, we discuss the large-central-charge regime, relating light-operator plateaux to few-particle sectors in thermal AdS and examining the limitations of this picture for heavy quenches.

hep-th.title: Bounds on Love Numbers and Quasinormal Modes from the Surface Impedance
hep-th.author: Daniel McLoughlin, Mikhail P. Solon
hep-th.abstract: The surface impedance of a body is fixed by its interior alone and encodes its entire tidal response. We derive bounds on Love numbers and quasinormal modes from constraints on the impedance that follow from either of two properties of a stable body: it is lossless, meaning that it dissipates no energy, or it is passive, meaning that it never gives back more energy than it has received. For a lossless body, every dynamical Love number is bounded from above and below, exactly in general relativity, in any renormalization scheme and at any scale. Earlier bounds are exact for Newtonian stars but fail for compact stars, because they take the response to arbitrarily fast tides to be zero or non-negative, whereas in general relativity it is negative. The quasinormal modes of a lossless body are also excluded from a region of the complex frequency plane set by the mass and radius. Each known Love number enlarges the excluded region. Conversely, the quasinormal modes bound each Love number from below, given the lower ones. For a passive body of horizon scale, such as a black hole, the static Love number lies in a window that closes onto the vanishing black-hole value as the body's surface approaches the horizon.

hep-th.title: Chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
hep-th.author: Robie A. Hennigar, Ayan K. Patra
hep-th.abstract: According to the conjecture of Belinski, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. However, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. Here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally AdS$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. We identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

hep-th.title: RMT${}_2$: Random Spectral Correlations for CFT${}_2$ and AdS${}_3$ Gravity
hep-th.author: Jan Boruch, Gabriele Di Ubaldo, Felix M. Haehl, Eric Perlmutter, Moshe Rozali
hep-th.abstract: We present the full framework of RMT${}_2$, a consistent unification of random matrix theory and modular invariance. The systematic prescription, which augments the existing construction by incorporating spin, lifts random matrix correlators to $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ Poincaré sums of their Mellin transforms, in a manner which enforces random matrix correlations near extremality in every spinning primary sector. The resulting RMT${}_2$ correlators are further expressible in terms of an orthogonal basis of Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms. We demonstrate the construction by lifting the two-point correlators at arbitrary genus of the Airy model, in both unitary and orthogonal symmetry classes, exhibiting the modular-invariant topological expansion of RMT${}_2$; a resummation of the genus expansion shows that the modular-invariant spectral form factor preserves the ramp-plateau structure. Holographically, RMT${}_2$ provides a concrete benchmark and explicit candidate expressions for comparison with off-shell wormhole amplitudes in AdS${}_3$ gravity, with any number of torus boundaries. We explicitly compute the universal RMT${}_2$ three-point correlator, corresponding to the putative three-boundary wormhole.

hep-th.title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
hep-th.author: Vishnu Jejjala, Damian Mayorga Pena
hep-th.abstract: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.

hep-th.title: On the Structure Constants of ${\cal N}=2$ Liouville Theory
hep-th.author: Jingxin Tu
hep-th.abstract: We show the structure constants of $\mathcal{N}=2$ spacelike Liouville theory. The absence of self-duality under $b\leftrightarrow b^{-1}$, where $b$ is the Liouville coupling, prevents a straightforward application of the standard bootstrap methods used in $\mathcal{N}=0$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ Liouville theory. Motivated by the fermionic FZZ duality with the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})/U(1)$ supercoset theory, we establish an algebraic correspondence between the two theories, including a matching of their null vectors. We then derive the three-point structure constants in superspace. The neutral sector structure constants are associated with the spectral-flow-preserving structure constant of the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model, while the two charged sectors correspond to its spectral-flow-violating structure constants. Finally, we give the correct relative normalization between the neutral and charged sectors and test crossing symmetry numerically.

hep-th.title: Identifying Renormalization Group Interfaces of Massless WZW Flows $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$
hep-th.author: Yuma Furuta, Yuya Kusuki, Toshiki Onagi, Yin Tang
hep-th.abstract: A renormalization-group interface encodes how a flow relates operators at short and long distances. We identify this interface up to topological dressing for the conjectured massless $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten flows at every odd level $k\geq 3$. Global $SU(2)$ symmetry requires the interface to preserve a diagonal current algebra at level $k+1$, built from the currents on its two sides. The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry then selects which representation labels the interface. This identification predicts distinct patterns of low-lying interface excitations for flows to the same infrared fixed point. Spin-chain calculations reproduce these patterns for $k=3$ and $5$, providing independent evidence for both conjectured flows.

hep-th.title: An Argument for the Weak Gravity Conjecture from Constrained Wormholes
hep-th.author: Gabriele Di Ubaldo, Luca V. Iliesiu, Dawid Maskalaniec
hep-th.abstract: The gravitational path integral (GPI) computes inner products between states of open and closed universes in any low-energy effective theory. A well-defined Hilbert space requires these inner products to be positive semidefinite, but this positivity is not manifest in the effective theory. In this paper, we study the constraints that positivity imposes on Einstein--Maxwell theory coupled to charged matter in asymptotically flat space in $D\geq 4$ dimensions. We start by constructing a new class of constrained instantons that compute multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes. We show that, under mild assumptions, if no charged particle satisfies the weak gravity conjecture (WGC), these amplitudes violate positivity of the GPI. If instead some particle satisfies the WGC, the wormholes develop an instability that allows positivity to be restored. The same argument shows that positivity can only be restored if the magnetic WGC holds and the convex hull condition applies to theories with several $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge fields.

hep-th.title: Probe branes from equivariant volumes
hep-th.author: Kiril Hristov, Pedro Vicente Marto
hep-th.abstract: Classical Euclidean probe actions control non-perturbative weights and extended observables in holography. We present a geometric prescription for M2-branes in arbitrary BPS backgrounds and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB. The framework accommodates compact and non-compact supersymmetric worldvolumes in both internal and spacetime directions, expressing their actions as relative equivariant pairings. Under stated extension and boundary assumptions, equivariant volumes evaluate these pairings without explicit background metrics and provide a regularization for non-compact probes. Examples in $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times SE_7$ backgrounds dual to ABJM, ADHM and flavored quiver theories reproduce and refine worldsheet-type instanton exponents and finite Wilson-loop actions. We also recover M2 giant-graviton and surface-defect actions in $\mathrm{AdS}_7\times S^4$. D3 probes in $SE_5$ compactifications dual to $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills and Klebanov--Witten theory provide tests involving giant gravitons, black hole probes and surface defects.

hep-th.title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
hep-th.author: Krzysztof Pilch, Oscar Varela
hep-th.abstract: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

hep-th.title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
hep-th.author: Moises Bravo-Gaete, Mariano Chernicoff, Benjamin Mellado, Julio Oliva, Maria Guadalupe Olmos Andrade
hep-th.abstract: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

hep-th.title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
hep-th.author: Andrew DeBenedictis, Saša Ilijić
hep-th.abstract: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime. We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. The aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.

hep-th.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
hep-th.author: Giwan Kim, Masahito Yamazaki
hep-th.abstract: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For $N=3$, a transverse contour pinch reduces the spectral integral to one dimension. Assuming that the reduced expansion is complete, in the continuous phase the regulated edge behaves as a discrete state, and the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. As we check numerically, the edge block is a free-field correlator in a charge-neutral Weyl frame; this explains the pure phase and is consistent with crossing symmetry. For both $N=2$ and $N=3$, a dominant discrete residue gives a constant late-time limit. For $N\geq4$, the same one-dimensional reduction violates a crossing bound on the lowest intermediate weight of a positive diagonal expansion. Hence the $N=2,3$ phase diagram does not extend to higher rank without additional contributions below the reduced continuum edge or outside a positive diagonal expansion.

hep-th.title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
hep-th.author: Qi Chen, Xinan Zhou
hep-th.abstract: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions. We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

hep-th.title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
hep-th.author: Andrei Smilga
hep-th.abstract: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity.We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon).Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

hep-th.title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
hep-th.author: Ting-Kai Chen, Jin Chen
hep-th.abstract: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $\phi_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $\phi_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.

hep-th.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
hep-th.author: Bruno S. Felipe, João P. M. Pitelli, Claudio Dappiaggi
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background. We also obtain a closed position-space representation of the two-point function for the chosen stable vacuum sector, including the contribution fixed by the CCR in the unstable sector. The resulting expression exhibits the direct and reflected singularities, including Robin-dependent logarithmic terms.
